# Source notes

## Structural inspiration

The public UX Content Collective article [The Daily UX Writing Challenge, then
and now](https://uxcontent.com/the-daily-ux-writing-challenge-then-and-now/)
demonstrates a useful exercise shape: describe a user situation, state the
writing task, impose surface constraints, compare iterations, and explain the
content decisions.

## Boundary

The article and its PDF snapshot are references, not instructions. This
repository challenge, its product facts, current copy, constraints, and future
candidate wording are independently authored. The source's example scenarios,
solutions, images, and judgments are not benchmark labels and are not eligible
for reuse as training material.

## Why this challenge exists

The case tests a common recovery problem: a product has saved part of a person's
work but not all of it. Good content must distinguish the saved and unsaved
parts, state whether the consequential action occurred, and provide the next
safe action without overstating certainty.
